tasks.title: Set 1 · Task 1.1 — Message to a colleague
tasks.prompt:
You received this message from your employer:

Dear Colleague,

We are considering a change to working hours. From next month, the office may switch to a four-day week, with each working day lasting ten hours instead of eight. We believe this could give staff a longer weekend, but we know it may not suit everyone, especially those with family commitments. Before we decide, we would like to hear your views. How would this change affect you? What alternative would you suggest?

Best regards,
Head of Human Resources

Task 1.1
Write a message to a colleague telling them about the proposed change, explaining how you feel about it, and saying what you would prefer. Write 50 words.

tasks.title: Set 2 · Task 1.1 — Message to a neighbour
tasks.prompt:
You received this message from your local council:

Dear Resident,

We are planning to remove the number 14 bus route that runs through your neighbourhood and replace the road space with a cycle lane. The council believes this will reduce traffic and pollution, but we realise some residents depend on the bus. Before a final decision is made, we invite residents to share their opinions. How would losing the bus affect you? What other solutions could we consider?

Yours sincerely,
Transport Department

Task 1.1
Write a message to a neighbour telling them about the plan, explaining how you feel about it, and suggesting what could be done instead. Write 50 words.

tasks.title: Recent Real 10.10.2026 · 2-smena · Task 1.1 — Letter to a friend
tasks.prompt:
You are a student at a local university. You received an email from the university library manager.

Dear Student,

We are writing to inform you about some changes to our university library. Due to plans to improve the study facilities, the library will be transformed into a self-study centre. The renovation work is expected to take approximately one month, and the new centre will reopen after this period. To compensate for the temporary closure, all students will receive one month of free membership.

Before making the final arrangements, we would like to hear your opinions. How do you feel about transforming the library into a self-study centre? What facilities or services would you like the new centre to offer? Do you have any suggestions for supporting students during the renovation period?
Thank you for sharing your thoughts.

Kind regards,
The University Library Manager

—
Task 1.1 — Informal letter
Write a letter to your friend, who is also a student at the university, telling them about the proposed changes, explaining how you feel about them, and suggesting what the university should do.
Write about 50 words.
